answer: Each agent's first output is hashed into a fingerprint in a shared ledger. When a new identity appears the chain diffs its output against the store; matching fingerprints within 24 hours flag a duplicate and freeze both. Attacker math turns ugly: a thousand-agent farm needs a thousand distinct outputs, and keeping them separate costs ~$2 an agent-hour on cloud, so a month of fakes runs ~$1.4M, past the payout. Trusting a fresh signature is like spotting a glacier; the real one took ten thousand years to take shape, while a cast of opal ice dropped into the ocean dissolves in a day.
